_meta.description: Global Import Quota / Tariff-Rate Quota (TRQ) database — seed data for the Import Quota scenario block
_meta.methodology: Records compiled from primary regulatory sources: WTO I-TIP, EUR-Lex, USITC HTS, UK Trade Tariff, national customs authorities. Verification levels: 'verified' = primary regulation text located and read; 'partial' = reliable secondary reference found but primary text not retrieved.
sources: WTO Integrated Trade Intelligence Portal (I-TIP): https://i-tip.wto.org/goods/
USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS), Chapter 99: https://hts.usitc.gov/

quotaTypes.global_aggregate: Single pool; all exporting countries compete equally on FCFS or pro-rata basis
quotaTypes.country_specific: Fixed volume reserved for a single named exporting country; no residual pool
quotaTypes.combined: Named country allocations for major suppliers plus a residual FCFS pool for others
quotaTypes.residual_fcfs: A residual pool distributed first-come-first-served after country-specific allocations are exhausted

legalBasis.primaryRegulation: Japan WTO Schedule LXXXVIII — Uruguay Round concession; 1994
legalBasis.mechanism: Simultaneous Buy-and-Sell (SBS) managed by MAFF / Agriculture and Livestock Industries Corporation (ALIC)
legalBasis.hsNote: Administered under the Staple Food Law (Law No. 112 of 1994)

volume.note: 682,200 t milled basis; set at 8% of 1986–88 domestic consumption per Uruguay Round. Japan has maintained at this level since 2000.

tariffsInQuota.note: Duty-free; managed through government SBS mechanism. Effectively captured via government mark-up on resale.

tariffsOutOfQuota.note: ¥341/kg (~700% ad valorem at prevailing world prices)

countryAllocations.note: Largest SBS quota holder; approx. 150,000–180,000 t p.a.
Other WTO members compete under the SBS scheme

effectiveDates.note: Ongoing WTO bound commitment; no sunset

quotas.notes: Out-of-quota rate is among the world's highest agricultural tariffs. Japan has consistently resisted tariffication pressure; MA quota is a practical ceiling on commercial rice trade.

legalBasis.primaryRegulation: Japan WTO Schedule LXXXVIII — Uruguay Round concession
legalBasis.mechanism: State Trading: imports managed by the Ministry of Agriculture / Farmland and Water Bureau (formerly Food Agency). Government buys at CIF world price; resells domestically with a mark-up (price stabilisation markup ≤ ¥17,060/t).
legalBasis.domesticLaw: Food Control Act (repealed 1994); now managed under Grain Management Law

volume.note: 5.74 MT WTO bound access; Japan's actual wheat imports typically exceed the TRQ volume at in-quota rates via state trading

tariffsInQuota.note: Technically duty-free at the border; effective protection delivered via government mark-up system

tariffsOutOfQuota.note: ¥55/kg = ¥55,000/t (approx. 150–250% ad valorem depending on world price)

countryAllocations.note: Approximately 50% of total; hard red winter / dark northern spring

legalBasis.primaryRegulation: Japan WTO Schedule LXXXVIII — Uruguay Round concession
legalBasis.mechanism: State trading; same government-managed mark-up system as wheat (MAFF/ALIC)

volume.note: 1.369 MT WTO bound access; includes malt barley and feed barley

countryAllocations.note: Largest supplier; feed and malting barley

quotas.product: Section 232 steel TRQ — South Korea (all steel products)
quotas.hsCodeRef: Chapter 72, 73 steel products listed in Annex I of Proclamation 9740

legalBasis.primaryRegulation: Presidential Proclamation 9740 of 22 April 2018 (establishing Korea TRQ under Section 232)
legalBasis.termination: Presidential Proclamation [2025] of 11 March 2025 — all Section 232 country-specific TRQs terminated effective 12 March 2025; 25% tariff restored on all Korean steel

volume.note: Set at 100% of Korea's average annual steel exports to US in 2015–2017 (~2.39 million metric tonnes); individual product-level quotas published in Proclamation 9740 Annex

tariffsInQuota.note: 0% — Korea was the only country exempted from the 25% S232 tariff for in-quota imports

tariffsOutOfQuota.note: 25% Section 232 tariff applied on all Korean steel above TRQ volume; now applies to all Korean steel post-termination

countryAllocations.note: Country-specific TRQ; all volume reserved for Korea. No residual pool for other origins.

effectiveDates.note: TERMINATED 12 March 2025 per Presidential Proclamation. Korean steel now subject to full 25% S232 tariff with no TRQ exemption.

quotas.notes: Korea TRQ was the only quota-based exemption from S232 steel tariffs; all others (Canada, Mexico, EU, UK, Japan, Australia, Argentina, Brazil) obtained full tariff exemptions or separate arrangements. Termination March 2025 was part of broader S232 tariff policy reset.

quotas.product: Section 232 steel TRQ — Brazil and Argentina (all steel products)

legalBasis.primaryRegulation: Presidential Proclamation 10328 (Brazil TRQ, 2022); Proclamation 9759 (Argentina TRQ, 2018)
legalBasis.termination: Both TRQs TERMINATED 12 March 2025; full 25% S232 tariff restored on Brazilian and Argentine steel

volume.note: Brazil: approx. 3.5 million t p.a. (set at 2018–2020 average); Argentina: approx. 135,000 t p.a. (small producer). Individual product-level volumes in proclamation annexes.

effectiveDates.note: TERMINATED 12 March 2025. Both countries now subject to full 25% S232 tariff.

sources.label: USTR: Section 232 investigations and country TRQs

quotas.notes: Terminated concurrently with Korea TRQ on 12 March 2025. Post-termination, Brazil and Argentina joined all other non-exempted countries in paying the full 25% S232 steel tariff.
